critical_code_review_comments: server.py now 2010 lines — continued growth past the 700-line guideline. Recommend splitting into routers/ modules (auth, invites, onboarding, ingest, inbox, contacts_profile, etc.). Same as iter12 note, still non-blocking.

InviteInput.phones has no format validation (any non-empty string accepted) — a stray '+91 abc' would be stored. For MVP fine because SMS delivery is mocked, but when Twilio is wired up, add E.164 validation (e.g. `re.match(r'^\+?[1-9]\d{7,14}$', p)`) or use pydantic constrained str.
POST /api/invites doesn't cap the number of phones per request — a client could POST 10k phones and inflate the tenant document unbounded. Add a reasonable max (e.g. 100 per call).
InviteInput uses a raw dict for each invite (phone/status/invited_at/invited_by) without a Pydantic model — refactor into `class Invite(BaseModel)` for consistency with other domain models.

Login.js is now 396 lines and packs auth + full 6-step wizard + upload + invites in one component. Consider splitting: components/onboarding/Step1Company.js, Step2Scale.js, Step3Software.js, Step4Connect.js, Step5Invite.js, Step6AI.js with a wizard state container.

In createWorkspace() a failing /onboarding/suggest is silently swallowed (empty catch) — that's fine per spec (falls back to DEFAULT_ROLES), but a low-priority console.warn would help debugging when the LLM budget is exhausted.

Step 4 tally/zoho tiles are labelled 'Coming soon' but are still styled as clickable-looking labels with `border border-dashed`. They correctly have no onClick, but a user might expect a tooltip on hover. Cosmetic UX polish.

Step 5 invite phone chips don't offer a remove/x button — once added, a user can't remove a wrong number without going back to the previous step (and back does not clear phones). Add a small ✕ per chip.

aiProgress useEffect (Login.js:138-143) resets to 0 whenever `step` changes to 6, but the timers array captured in closure is cleared only in cleanup — if the component re-renders during animation, timers may leak. Minor React housekeeping.
